series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator. The swap cache allocator is used by zswap writeback to allocate a folio that can be freed directly once writeback completes, without being on the LRU. This change allows for more flexibility in managing swap cache folios and prevents potential issues with synchronous devices or asynchronous ones. The patch updates several files, including mm/swap.h and mm/swap_state.c, to reflect this change.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/3] mm: swap: drop dropbehind swap cache folios on writeback completion
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the Linux kernel to drop swap cache folios from their cache once writeback completes, rather than leaving them for reclaim to find later. This is achieved by setting a flag on the write operation and dropping the folio directly in the folio_end_writeback() function. The change extends existing functionality for file folios to also include swap cache folios. The patch modifies several kernel files, including mm/filemap.c, mm/page_io.c, mm/swap_state.c, and mm/vmscan.c.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 3/3] mm: zswap: drop cold writeback folios via swap dropbehind
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the zswap writeback process by dropping cold folios from the swap cache after they are written back to disk, rather than leaving them on the LRU for reclaim. This is done by allocating the folio off the LRU and marking it PG_dropbehind, which allows the swap dropbehind path to free the folio once writeback completes. The patch aims to reduce memory residency time for cold pages and improve system performance.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2] mm/huge_memory: add folio_reset_partially_mapped()
patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function called folio_reset_partially_mapped() to the Linux kernel's huge_memory module. The function is responsible for resetting the PG_partially_mapped flag and updating the MTHP_STAT_NR_ANON_PARTIALLY_MAPPED stat when a folio is partially mapped. The patch extracts this common logic from two existing functions, __folio_unqueue_deferred_split() and __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped(), to improve code organization and maintainability. The function asserts that the folio is frozen before performing these operations, ensuring that deferred split cannot set the flag again under it. This change aims to simplify the code and make it more efficient.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v5 00/19] selftests/mm: improve khugepaged coverage

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 01/19] selftests/mm: raise the khugepaged test-case cap
series_items.patch_summary: This patch increases the maximum number of test cases for the khugepaged selftest from 64 to 256, allowing more tests to be run without aborting the suite prematurely.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 02/19] selftests/mm: skip collapse_compound_extreme() where the PMD is too large
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the selftests/mm/khugepaged.c test to skip a specific test case where the PMD (Page Map Directory) size is too large, causing the allocator to fail reliably handing out allocations. The test case in question, collapse_compound_extreme(), requires multiple consecutive PMD-order allocations, which becomes unmanageable with larger PMDs. By skipping this test case for PMDs larger than 32M, the patch ensures that the test suite does not fail abruptly and allows other cases to run successfully.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 03/19] selftests/mm: scale khugepaged's collapse wait with the PMD size
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adjusts the timeout for khugepaged's collapse wait to be proportional to the size of the PMD (Page Map Directory). The original three-second timeout was too short for large PMDs, leading to test failures. The new approach scales the timeout by adding one second for every 128M bytes collapsed, ensuring that larger PMDs have a longer wait time. This change improves the reliability of khugepaged tests on systems with large page sizes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 04/19] selftests/mm: skip khugepaged page cache cases without a PMD folio
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the selftests/mm module to skip khugepaged page cache cases that do not support PMD folios. The issue arises from a limitation in the page cache, which caps folio order at MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, below the PMD order on certain architectures. As a result, the kernel refuses collapses for PMD-sized pages, leading to test failures. To address this, the patch introduces a new function thp_file_supported_orders() to determine supported orders and skips shmem and file mem types where the cap is below the PMD order. This ensures that tests are only run on architectures that support PMD folios.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 05/19] selftests/mm: make the swap cases' swapout reliable
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the reliability of swapout operations in selftests/mm by introducing a retry mechanism to handle cases where MADV_PAGEOUT is best effort and khugepaged may still be working on the range. The patch adds a new function `swapout_range` that retries swapping out a range up to two seconds, holding the range out of khugepaged's reach meanwhile. If the pages still won't swap out after retrying, the test will skip this step as it is not a kernel bug. This change aims to fix issues on arm64 with 64K pages where the case loses the race between swapping out and khugepaged collapsing the range.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 06/19] selftests/mm: stop khugepaged during the MADV_COLLAPSE cases
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the selftests/mm/khugepaged.c file to stop khugepaged during MADV_COLLAPSE cases by clearing per-order controls in addition to global controls. This is necessary because khugepaged was interfering with the test cases, causing them to fail due to unexpected page collapses. The patch sets the per-order controls to 'inherit' instead of 'never', allowing MADV_COLLAPSE on shmem to still find an order to build pages. This change fixes a problem introduced by a previous patch and ensures that the test cases run correctly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 07/19] selftests/mm: move is_backed_by_folio() into vm_util
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the function `is_backed_by_folio()` from `split_huge_page_test.c` to `vm_util.c`. The function checks if an address range is backed by a folio of a given order, which is useful for tests that build or collapse large folios. The move allows other tests to use this functionality without duplicating code. No functional changes are made.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 08/19] selftests/mm: add folio-order check for address ranges
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function called is_range_backed_by_order() to the selftests/mm module, which checks if a given address range is backed by folios of a specific order. The function verifies that every folio-sized, folio-aligned part of the range maps one folio of the target order, head to tail, with the head at the start of the part. This patch addresses a limitation in existing functions such as is_backed_by_folio() and check_huge_anon(), which only account for single-page or PMD mappings, respectively. The new function will be used by an mTHP collapse test to determine if a range is backed by folios of the target order, allowing it to distinguish between collapsed and non-collapsed ranges.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 09/19] selftests/mm: add folio-order detection self-check
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a self-test to verify the accuracy of the vm_util folio-order helpers, is_backed_by_folio() and is_range_backed_by_order(). The test faults in memory for each supported anonymous huge page order, enabling only that order, and checks if the helpers correctly report the backing order. This ensures that the khugepaged mTHP tests are reliable. The test has been verified on x86-64 and arm64 architectures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 10/19] selftests/mm: add khugepaged completion barrier helper
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a helper function called khugepaged_full_pass() to the hugepage_settings module in selftests/mm. The function is used to wait for a full pass of khugepaged, which is necessary to distinguish between 'not collapsed' and 'not scanned yet' states in khugepaged tests. It uses sysfs to wake up the khugepaged daemon and waits until it completes one pass. The patch also modifies thp_write_settings() to write khugepaged settings only when their values change, preventing new passes from starting. This is necessary because a store to either sleep knob wakes up the daemon, causing it to start a new pass if the pages_to_scan value covers every mm on the list.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 11/19] selftests/mm: add order-parameterized khugepaged collapse cases
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds four new test cases to the selftests/mm/khugepaged context, which checks how the khugepaged collapse mechanism handles different scenarios. The new cases are order-parameterized and check for specific behaviors such as collapsing a populated window, handling partial windows with one present PTE, and mixed sources that are already large folios of a smaller order. Each case faults its region before MADV_HUGEPAGE with only the target order enabled to ensure that the result comes from khugepaged. The test cases wait for a full pass rather than waiting for the result to appear, as without a completed pass 'not collapsed' and 'not scanned yet' are indistinguishable.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 12/19] selftests/mm: parameterize the mixed-source collapse case by source order
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mixed-source collapse case in the selftests/mm suite to parameterize the source order by adding a new option -s, which specifies the source order alongside the target order -c. The test faults at the specified source order and collapses contpte-mapped sources into larger mTHP if possible. This change allows for more flexible testing of memory huge page (mHP) behavior on different architectures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 13/19] selftests/mm: cover a shared-source collapse write race
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series adds a selftest to cover a shared-source collapse write race in the kernel. The test checks that CoW isolation survives a collapse racing with writes to the shared source by having the parent unshare one page every 10ms while the child collapses. This is preparation for changing how collapse handles fork-shared sources.

review_comments.summary: Addressed two issues flagged by Sashiko: closing sync[0] to prevent fd leak and handling wstatus correctly in case waitpid() fails.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 14/19] selftests/mm: run every supported collapse order by default
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged selftest to run all supported collapse orders by default, rather than just one order when specified with the -c option. The test now runs each mTHP case once per supported anon THP order below the PMD, and includes both orders as array indices and shift counts. The patch also updates the usage message to reflect these changes and adds range checking for the -s and -c options.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 15/19] selftests/mm: check that one khugepaged pass collapses one window
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new selftest to verify that the khugepaged daemon collapses one window in one pass. The test prepares an aligned window, records its source PFNs from pagemap, runs one full pass of khugepaged, and checks that the window came out collapsed with exactly one collapse attempt attributed to it. The test also verifies that the scan_sleep_millisecs is set to a minute to prevent the test from taking too long. This patch has been tested on x86-64 4K and arm64 64K architectures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 16/19] selftests/mm: add khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a selftest harness to exercise khugepaged under contention from multiple threads, simulating various scenarios such as faults, GUP pins, fork, mremap, and MADV_DONTNEED operations on the same address space. The test checks that a racing page reads either its original pattern or zero, and includes assertions in the kernel for additional verification.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that mremap() frees the scratch area, which must be re-reserved for the next cycle, and provided a fix to claim it again using mmap().

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 17/19] selftests/mm: race the collapse of windows with holes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a selftest to the Linux kernel that tests the collapse of huge pages with holes under racing conditions. The test harness simulates two scenarios: one where all PTEs are present and another where there are holes in the window. It runs both scenarios for each driver mode, including stepped and madvise modes. The test checks for corruption and reports the results.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 18/19] selftests/mm: add memory-pressure threads to the khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds two new threads to the khugepaged race harness: pageout and compactor. The pageout thread simulates memory pressure by repeatedly advising a region of pages for swap-out, faults them back in, and checks their contents to ensure they remain unchanged after being swapped out. The compactor thread writes to /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory in a loop, competing with the collapse for pages it is gathering. Each combination of mode and occupancy limit is run with and without these threads, testing whether the khugepaged system can handle memory pressure and compaction simultaneously without introducing corruption.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 19/19] selftests/mm: zap whole PTE tables in the khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged race harness to occasionally zap whole PMD-aligned areas of page tables, rather than just individual pages or tables. This is done to test a specific scenario where a collapse walks the same table as another process zapping it. The change aims to improve the robustness and testing of the kernel's memory management features.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series improves the coverage of khugepaged tests by addressing several gaps in testing. It makes the test suite run at a 512M PMD, detects results per window rather than count, drives khugepaged deterministically, covers collapse at every supported order, and races collapse against various sources. The patches also include changes to comments, changelogs, and helper names for clarity and consistency. The tests have been run on an unmodified kernel with various configurations and show no failures.

review_comments.summary: The author acknowledged that the khugepaged test case collapse_compound_extreme() fails on a 512M PMD due to unreliable allocation of hpage_pmd_nr PMD-order allocations, and agreed to skip this case where the PMD is larger than 32M.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

collapse_compound_extreme() builds a PTE table full of distinct PTE-mapped
compound pages by cycling hpage_pmd_nr fault-time THPs through mremap.  It
therefore needs hpage_pmd_nr PMD-order allocations in a row.  That is fine
at a 2M PMD (4K base pages) or a 32M one (16K).  A 512M PMD -- arm64 with
64K base pages -- makes each of those an order-13 allocation, which the
allocator cannot reliably hand out even once, let alone 8192 times.

The failure is not a quiet one: the case calls ksft_exit_fail_msg(), so the
whole binary stops and every case after it is lost.

Skip the case where the PMD is larger than 32M.  The MADV_COLLAPSE cases
still cover PMD-order collapse on those configurations, and 4K and 16K
PMDs are unaffected.

review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the wait_for_scan() function's timeout being too short for large PMDs on arm64. They explained that the timeout is a ceiling on a poll loop, not a sleep, and provided data showing that raising it costs nothing to passing cases. The author proposed keeping three seconds as the floor and adding a second per 128M collapsed.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

wait_for_scan() gives every case the same three seconds, whatever the huge
page costs to build.  collapse_full() asks for four of them: 8M at a 2M
PMD, but 2G at a 512M PMD -- arm64 with 64K base pages.  Three seconds is
thin at that size, and the case has reported a failure for a collapse that
was still going.

The timeout is a ceiling on a poll loop, not a sleep: the loop stops as
soon as ops->check_huge() sees the collapse, or as soon as full_scans has
advanced by two.  Raising it costs a passing case nothing.  Across 80 runs
of collapse_full() on arm64 with 64K pages the wait was half a second in
73 of them, with a tail to two seconds.

Keep three seconds as the floor and add a second per 128M collapsed.  A 2M
PMD is unchanged, so x86-64 is too; a 512M PMD gets 19 seconds.

On arm64 with 64K pages a passing ./khugepaged all:anon takes 49 seconds
under TCG before and after this change.

review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

An mTHP collapse test needs to know that a range is backed by folios of the
target order, and that they sit where a collapse would put them.  Nothing
answers that today: is_backed_by_folio() classifies the folio behind a
single page, and check_huge_anon() reads smaps AnonHugePages, which only
accounts PMD mappings.

Add is_range_backed_by_order().  It requires every folio-sized, folio-
aligned part of the range to map one folio of that order, head to tail,
with the head at the start of the part.

A part backed by two smaller folios fails, and so does a folio mapped off
its natural alignment.  The mTHP cases need both to tell a collapsed range
from the one beside it.

Assisted-by: LLM
Reviewed-by: Mike Rapoport (Microsoft) <rppt@kernel.org>

 2 files changed, 49 insertions(+)

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
index 3ea42a7a2a3e..4947612e8b3d 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
@@ -552,6 +552,53 @@ bool is_backed_by_folio(char *vaddr, int order, int pagemap_fd,
 	return false;
 }
 
+/**
+ * is_range_backed_by_order() - check that a range is backed by @order folios
+ * @start: start of the range, a multiple of the folio size
+ * @len: length of the range in bytes, a multiple of the folio size
+ * @order: the folio order to check for
+ * @pagemap_fd: open /proc/<pid>/pagemap of the range's owner
+ * @kpageflags_fd: open /proc/kpageflags
+ *
+ * Every folio-sized, folio-aligned part of the range must map one folio of
+ * @order, head to tail, with the head at the start of the part.  A part
+ * backed by several smaller folios fails, and so does a folio mapped off
+ * its natural alignment.
+ *
+ * Returns: true if the whole range is backed that way, false otherwise.
+ */
+bool is_range_backed_by_order(char *start, size_t len, int order,
+			      int pagemap_fd, int kpageflags_fd)
+{
+	const unsigned long nr_pages = 1UL << order;
+	const size_t folio_size = nr_pages * psize();
+	char *vaddr;
+
+	if ((uintptr_t)start % folio_size || len % folio_size)
+		return false;
+
+	for (vaddr = start; vaddr < start + len; vaddr += folio_size) {
+		const unsigned long pfn = pagemap_get_pfn(pagemap_fd, vaddr);
+		unsigned long i;
+
+		/* Not present, or a tail page */
+		if (pfn == -1UL || pfn % nr_pages)
+			return false;
+
+		for (i = 1; i < nr_pages; i++) {
+			char *page = vaddr + i * psize();
+
+			if (pagemap_get_pfn(pagemap_fd, page) != pfn + i)
+				return false;
+		}
+
+		if (!is_backed_by_folio(vaddr, order, pagemap_fd, kpageflags_fd))
+			return false;
+	}
+
+	return true;
+}

review_comments.summary: Author addressed a concern about potential compiler warnings due to implicit type conversions in minmax.h, proposed an alternative solution using explicit u32 types for the shift operation, and offered to re-spin v6 with the change.
review_comments.raw_body:
It does build: GCC 15 and clang 21, at -O2 and -Os, without a warning.

But the reason is not obvious.

ilog2() on a runtime u32 returns int, and minmax.h only accepts an int
against a u32 when __is_nonneg() can prove it non-negative at compile
time.

__ilog2_u32() is fls(n) - 1, so that proof only exists because the
if (entries) guard lets the compiler see entries != 0 through the inlined
fls().

But this is fragile. If a compiler does not get there, or a later change
that moves the guard, it turns it into a BUILD_BUG_ON.

Rather than a max_t() cast, we can give the shift its type first:

	if (entries) {
		new_ceiling = ilog2(entries);
		new_ceiling = max(new_ceiling, floor);
	} else if (is_kdump_kernel()) {

Two u32s, nothing left for the compiler to prove, same result.

If it looks good, I can re-spin v6 with the change.

Thanks for the review and the test!

From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

collapse_scan_pmd() and collapse_run_pmd() each have a clear locking
contract.  The scan is called with mmap_lock held for reading and returns
with it still held.  The collapse is called without it.

collapse_single_pmd() kept that boundary inside itself.  It dropped the
lock on some paths and not others, and reported which by way of a bool its
callers had to carry along and then act on.

Open-code it in the two callers.  Each scans under the lock it already
holds and, on SCAN_SUCCEED, gives the lock up before running the collapse.
khugepaged's lock_dropped and madvise_collapse()'s mmap_unlocked both go:
the code dropping the lock is now the code that wanted to know.

khugepaged's walk carries on to the next table while the scan keeps
refusing, and ends once a collapse has taken the lock from under it.
madvise_collapse() re-finds its VMA after a collapse, which it did before,
and now uses a NULL vma to say that it has to.  It still reports the drop
to its own caller, from the line that does it.

The lock is given up and taken again at the same points as before.  No
functional change.

On Tue, Sep 08, 2026 at 10:19:44AM +0100, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> On Mon, Sep 07, 2026 at 02:56:26PM -0700, Nicolin Chen wrote:
> > On Mon, Sep 07, 2026 at 10:58:34AM +0100, Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) wrote:
> > 
> > I still think that cmdq_max_n_shift can slightly tidy things here.
> > 
> > > +static u32 arm_smmu_queue_max_n_shift(u32 ceiling, u32 ent_sz_shift,
> > > +				      u32 entries)
> > 
> > Here, all three inputs would have been "shifts", instead of two
> > "shifts" and one "number of entries".
> > 
> > > +{
> > > +	u32 floor = PAGE_SHIFT - ent_sz_shift;
> > > +
> > > +	if (!entries)
> > > +		return ceiling;
> > > +
> > > +	return min(ceiling, max(ilog2(entries), floor));
> > 
> > And I see Sashiko keeps complaining against the ilog2 here:
> 
> It does build: GCC 15 and clang 21, at -O2 and -Os, without a warning.
> 
> But the reason is not obvious.
> 
> ilog2() on a runtime u32 returns int, and minmax.h only accepts an int
> against a u32 when __is_nonneg() can prove it non-negative at compile
> time.
> 
> __ilog2_u32() is fls(n) - 1, so that proof only exists because the
> if (entries) guard lets the compiler see entries != 0 through the inlined
> fls().
> 
> But this is fragile. If a compiler does not get there, or a later change
> that moves the guard, it turns it into a BUILD_BUG_ON.
> 
> Rather than a max_t() cast, we can give the shift its type first:
> 
> 	if (entries) {
> 		new_ceiling = ilog2(entries);
> 		new_ceiling = max(new_ceiling, floor);
> 	} else if (is_kdump_kernel()) {
> 
> Two u32s, nothing left for the compiler to prove, same result.
> 
> If it looks good, I can re-spin v6 with the change.

It looks probably okay.. though I still don't get why you aren't
picking the straightforward "max_n_shift" over "max_entries".

max_n_shift is used by both HW and SW, and it does not have such
converting problem or need min/max, making the code cleaner :-/

Nicolin
